text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- A senior Agriculture Ministry official blamed Wednesday what he described as irresponsible political forces for stirring up hysteria in recent weeks, to the considerable detriment of agricultural producers. @

- Under a new reform of the pensions system worked out by the ministries of finance and welfare, the state would underwrite guarantees regarding capital and its yield up to the sum of frozen claims, kept in accounts at private funds.
- A report on the financial management of Hungarian State Railways by the company's management board calls for further investigation involving outside consultants.
- Bus drivers staged a two-hour warning strike in Pecs on Wednesday after union representatives and company executives failed to agree on this year's wage increase. @

- Visiting Slovak Justice Minister Jozef Liscak said it is unnecessary to promote the implementation of Council of Europe recommendations or elements of the Hungarian-Slovak basic treaty regarding minority rights, as Bratislava has already taken these into consideration.
- Production in Hungarian industry increased by 2.3 percent last year as against 1995, according to a report by the Central Statistical Office.
- Due to legal problems, the general meeting of the ceramics manufacturer Zalakeramia delayed a decision yesterday regarding a capital increase. @
- A 29 percent stake in the used goods trading and pawnship chain BAV will be sold via a closed tender in the near future.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The parliamentary commission investigating the Tocsik case presented a draft report to MPs accusing the former State Privatisation & Holding board chairman and the legal counselor of violating their official positions in proposing Tocsik as consultant. It also says that political responsibility rests with the then privatisation minister. @
- Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal was received by South African President Nelson Mandela and other senior state officials in Cape Town on Wednesday.

- A future network of suppliers for the bus manufacturer Ikarus may be built up in unemployment-stricken northern Hungary if the government accepts an initiative from Gabor Szeles, president of both Ikarus and the electronics company Videoton Rt.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- Romanian Foreign Ministry State Secretary Dumitru Ciousu is to visit Budapest in late February for talks on issues linked to NATO integration, said Romania's foreign affairs spokesman.

- No acceptable bid was submitted in the tender to privatise the power plants Pecsi Eromu, Bakonyi Eromu and Vertesi Eromu. Gyula Lengyel, president and CEO of national Electricity firm MVM said that the failure of the plants may hinder the privatisation of MVM due this year.
- The wine producer Egervin is expected to embark on the stock exchange within the next 18 months. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The government's concept of motorway construction needs revision as the present concessionary system puts excessive burdens on motorists, said Transport Minister Karoly Lotz.
- Following the sale of MOL shares due in a few weeks, a considerable package of the stocks of Richter will be offered for sale in April, the State Privatisation and Holding Co. said.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
